options: A tool that visualises analytical results
Essentially where information comes from, such as a spreadsheet, a company database or social media posts
A method for compressing large files
A policy governing who may access data
A machine learning model that predicts outcomes
questions.explanation: A data source is where your information comes from; it can be a list of customer names in a spreadsheet, sales details in a database, or tweets on social media, and can range from simple text files to large databases.

questions.stem: Which of the following are named as examples of relational databases that can act as data sources?
options: Amazon S3 and Azure Blob Storage
questions.explanation: MySQL, PostgreSQL and Oracle are cited as relational databases where data is organised in tables. MongoDB and Cassandra are NoSQL examples.

questions.stem: MongoDB and Cassandra are given as examples of which kind of data source?
options: NoSQL databases that may store data in more flexible formats
questions.explanation: MongoDB and Cassandra are NoSQL databases, which may store data in more flexible formats than the tables of a relational database.

questions.stem: Which type of data source is represented by systems such as Salesforce, SAP or Oracle ERP?
options: Business or enterprise applications like CRM and ERP systems
questions.explanation: Salesforce, SAP and Oracle ERP are business or enterprise applications (CRM and ERP systems) used to manage customer and operations data, serving as rich sources for analytics and BI.

questions.stem: In which environments are spreadsheet files such as Excel or Google Sheets described as especially common data sources?
options: Large-scale, highly technical enterprise environments only
questions.explanation: Spreadsheet files store data in tabular form and are common data sources especially in smaller-scale or less technical environments.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a flat file used as a data source?
questions.explanation: Flat files include CSV and text files: simple text files that store data in a structured format and are commonly used for data exchange and storage.

questions.stem: Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage and Microsoft Azure Blob Storage are examples of which data source category?
options: Cloud storage services used to store large amounts of data accessible from anywhere
questions.explanation: These are cloud storage platforms used to store large amounts of data in the cloud, accessible from anywhere.

questions.stem: What purpose do logs (system, application and web server logs) serve as a data source?
options: They provide raw data about usage and performance for monitoring, debugging and security analysis
They store customer contact details for marketing
They hold financial ledgers for accounting
They organise data into relational tables for BI
They provide tabular data for offline spreadsheet analysis
questions.explanation: Logs supply raw data about the usage and performance of systems and are used for monitoring, debugging and security analysis.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a category of data source in information systems?
questions.explanation: The listed categories are databases, business/enterprise applications, spreadsheet files, flat files, cloud storage and logs. Printed paper archives are not among them.

questions.stem: How do data integration, data analytics and data science each relate to data sources?
options: All three delete data sources after use
Integration brings different sources together; analytics helps you understand what the data is telling you; data science uses more complex methods to uncover deeper insights and make predictions
Integration predicts the future; analytics stores data; data science compresses it
Only data science uses data sources; the other two do not
Integration visualises data; analytics governs it; data science archives it
questions.explanation: Data integration combines different sources, data analytics interprets what the data says, and data science applies more complex methods to find deeper insights and make predictions from those sources.
